GANCHOS: A) Your cake collapses because you open the oven too early. | B) Why does a cake fall? | C) The oven door mistake. | escolhido: A

Your cake collapses because you open the oven too early. Science explains why.

When batter hits the heat, the leavening releases gas. The gas forms bubbles, and the cake rises.

In the first twenty minutes, the structure is still fragile. The egg proteins and the starch have not set yet.

If you open the door, cold air rushes in. The temperature drops, the bubbles shrink, and the middle sinks.

So the rule is simple. Do not open the oven before three quarters of the baking time has passed.

To check if it is done, push a toothpick into the center. If it comes out clean, take the cake out.

Let it cool for ten minutes before removing it from the pan. The structure firms up and the cake does not break.

Try it on your next recipe. Cake or no cake? Send this to a friend who loves to bake.
